The recent introductions that are part of the Annual Syllabus are made of different learning trends that mix the new advances in education with old conceptions about education that influence in great extent the learning process. Constructivism is essential to comprehend the nature of learning in which the students acquire the most active role being their needs and motivation key elements while learning. As stated by Fosnot (2005), constructivism opposes behaviorism or skills as the goal of instruction, cognitive development and profound understanding are seen not as maturation but as constructions of active learner reorganization. Fosnot (2005) continues adding that it is not a linear process and it emerges from the cognitive science, particularly the later work of Piaget just prior to his death and the socio-historical work of Vygotsky. Piaget (1958) and Vygotsky (1978) help determine the true nature of learning as a process. Fosnot (2005) recognizes that in Piaget

s theory it is found the most useful guide to think about adult-child relationships since adults are crucial in determining through daily interactions the nature of the socio-moral atmosphere where the young child lives in.

Linguistic Communication Competence as linked to the English language acquisition in this Annual syllabus is the ability needed to express, infer and interpret information using the linguistic code but also the sociolinguistic and pragmatic methods.
This competence is very important in this context since the students should communicate fluently in the foreign language and express themselves on a daily basis with no difficulties.

Mathematical Competence is the competence that works not only the numbers but also the logic and spatial thinking and it also includes competences in science and technology. It is the ability to interpret the natural world through the scientific method. In the present Annual Syllabus it acquires great importance when inferring information, using numbers and logic spatial elements to understand the basic grammar rules.

Digital Competence is essential in the current Annual Syllabus since society is going through a process of globalization and the use of the communication and information resources. It is part of the cross-curricular topics and it is essential for the students to know and apply their ICTs strategies to cope with the present global change, to keep informed and updated. Apart from that, smartphones are a reality today and it is necessary to train students in their correct use to include educative topics and make the students learn in a new and interesting way adapted to our times. It is also important to make them prepared to face an
world with the basic abilities to discard what is not useful or obsolete.

Learning to Learn Competence refers to the ability the students have to use their own cognitive resources to learn. Metacognition is a key aspect since they have to know about their own mental and psychological process and use it in benefit of their learning process. It refers to the capacity the students have to elaborate their own notes, links, the way they decide to remember concepts or understand the subject. All the mental system they create themselves to cope with their own study.

Foreign language learning develops Social and Civic Competences. It promotes and encourages the social skills required for co-operation and mutual understanding in real-life situations. Through the use of discussions, simulations, role plays and varied real-world tasks, this Syllabus enables students to improve their communication strategies and their ability to work together in pairs and groups. In addition, cross-cultural skills are taught through a series of awareness-raising practical activities as no language can be truly learnt without cultural understanding. The limited usage of the learners
mother tongue in class helps develop an atmosphere in which the foreign language becomes a genuine means of communication and cultural appreciation.

Sense of Initiative and Entrepreneurship is an essential key competence as it builds autonomy, creativity, responsibility and critical judgment. The foreign language class and this Annual Syllabus in particular contribute to materialize this competence by real-life tasks that require planning, management, problem-solving, and decision-making skills both in individual and in group projects. Speaking and writing activities encourage students to express their own opinions and present their ideas to the class promoting a pro-active learning atmosphere.

emerges from the ability to appreciate creativity in different types of artistic expression including music, performing arts, literature, and the visual arts.

The present Annual Syllabus is designed according to the new educational trends and methodologies that are formed by the Communicative Approach, Task-Based Learning and the Action-Oriented Approach that the CERFL establishes. To describe the Communicative Approach it is important to highlight the importance of language as a means for communication and social interaction. The Communicative Approach appeared in the 1970s and early 1980s due to the great demand of language teaching and the pressure on educators to change their methods. This Annual Syllabus is designed according to the idea that the student should be provided with the basic tools to express in a language being an active player in society able to interact in his daily basis.
The Task-Based Learning appeared from the Communicative approach and Sir William H. Kilpatrick was the founder of the concept itself making it famous through

in 1918. This method which is student-centered combines the role of the students being playing an active role in their education and according to their needs and characteristics, with a dynamic classroom approach to learn through actions, learning by doing. Within this learning the student can discover the world through games, real-world challenges, problem solving, etc. that make the learning enjoyable. This Annual Syllabus includes those challenges to work language and content in an easy and pleasant way for the student to discover the world through the necessary tools always taking the errors as a new opportunity to learn and improve.

The Action-Oriented Approach is also important to understand this Annual Syllabus. This approach emerged from the publication of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL), after twenty years of research to provide a solid, transparent, and comprehensible basis for the creation of language syllabus and guidelines. This approach considers the student to be a social agent in society in which he is the protagonist in his learning carrying out diverse real tasks using the necessary tools to succeed. The linguistic tasks are extensively used in this Annual Syllabus while the communicative and general competencies are the final objective assessed by rubrics. The students become independent language users through the daily actions they carry out in real contexts of life. The CEFRL encourages the teacher to help the students become autonomous in their learning, while learning by doing as social agents in common situations able to use the necessary tools to complete their different tasks successfully.

p.hi: The official regulations establish the contents so the topics have been selected depending on them. It always takes into account the characteristics of the classroom group which is essential to carry out a learning that pays attention to comprehension and diversity. The first term includes topics that are familiar to the student

s reality; the topics of the second and third term make the student know the world inside them but also the unknown, exploring new worlds and situations that are interesting for them, more complex ideas with a brief revision of the previous contents included. Topics are chosen making the student feel motivated, especially at the end of the year when the students need to be more motivated to finish successfully.
Topic 1 includes personal descriptions. It refers to all related to human nature (body parts, personal information, and explains how to address people, greetings, meetings, etc.)
Topic 2 focuses on the school and its features (building, teachers, students, and also classroom material).
Topic 3 focuses on Home and it refers to all related to the house as building (rooms), but also items found at home and how to invite someone giving directions.
Topic 4 focuses on shops, merchandising, clothes, supermarket and money. The student learns how to pay in pounds.
Topic 5 approaches the student to nature. The student learns different ecological ways of living and the most important natural disasters and daily problems such as global warming.
Topic 6 tries to give the student a cultural background. The student learns about different countries and learns different ways of communicating with people abroad(e-mail, letters, etc.).
Topic 7 explains how to get fit, how to be healthy through sports and the student learns about different illness
Topic 8 focuses on eating time, habits, and routines. The student learns about culinary traditions in different countries and learns about local gastronomy.

The design of the present Annual Syllabus is made to cater the different intelligences of the students, taking into account their personal characteristics with a personalized attention but also their needs as students and humans. It also tries to provide the students with the needed knowledge to acquire the different Key Competences but always in a communicative and dynamic way, a way which can be motivating for them, to learn through games and real life activities in which the student is able to know the world around, meet other cultures and learn from each other as students. To make every lesson enjoyable, fun and interactive working in pairs, group, or combining it through the units. All the skills are met in this Annual Syllabus and the students are able to work and study in an autonomous way.
To finish, the school and context have been of prime importance in the design of this Annual Syllabus since it is all shaped around the student

s educative environment. The syllabus tries to recreate through its design the heterogeneous, inclusive and participative atmosphere of the school in which all the members of the school community play an important role with a very active participation. The topics are adapted to the school

s characteristics with different tasks and activities that cater for all diversities, giving the student the idea that they are all part of this system, of this globalization and that their contribution
significant and important to continue growing in this world. English as a tool, as a medium and also as a goal is the essence of this syllabus.

This master has contributed a lot to our knowledge as teachers about the world around us and about the students. It contributes to our preparation as future teachers in order to work and instruct the future generations. It has been of great importance the fact that this master provides its students with the history that has developed around the concept of the English as tool for teaching next generations. How the educational system has developed in the last decades and the changes we are facing. It has been important in the sense that we must be aware of the constant changes that it implies as law, as a medium, as a tool and as a way of life. Teaching must be flexible and adapted to the current times. This is the reason why this syllabus is created based upon all the ideals and actual needs of education. Attention to diversity is of prime importance in learning since we, as teachers, must be aware that not just one method is valid. We must be eclectic and adapt our own knowledge and techniques to the specific requirements that the situation presents. It hasn

t been easy to elaborate a syllabus that attends all the possible variability that can be presented. Series of resources and materials have contributed to make the learning adapted to all the students, been always enjoyable and accessible for the learners to acquire the knowledge and information that establishes the syllabus and the law.

Furthermore, the fact that many members of the educational community have been met and known including students, their parents, department, etc. have contributed to the real experience in English teaching. This has been the expected experience required to have a good knowledge of this master and how the educational community is formed. It has been of real help to get in touch with all the laws, documents, and different syllabuses, since in that moment is when a teacher can really understand the real meaning of teaching not only as a medium to instruct but also to be part of the system. This allows me to grow as a person, as a professional.

Not only this has been a very positive and strongly recommended experience for students, this master also prepares us for the future as competent teachers. UNED offers a no-classroom education which may be difficult due to the different methodologies it presents. Since many of us have chosen this master because of work or family issues, little time can be employed to the full-time work this master requires but it always offers facilities for us, the students, to adapt our lives to the study.
